note: User word containing Greek character 'ϗ' (U+03D7) makes the English rules (dictionary.c TranslateRules) emit phonSWITCH followed by 'el' into word_phonemes (p); this tainted marker drives the translator2 switch logic.
SetTranslator2("el") allocates the secondary Greek translator (translator2) and sets translator2_language="el".
translator2 (Greek) is passed as the active translator 'tr' of a nested TranslateWord call that is still executing when translator2 is later freed.
Nested single-character word 'ϗ' (word_length==1 and FLAG_TRANSLATOR2) is spelled as an individual letter, with tr == the Greek translator2.
TranslateLetter for 'ϗ' looks up the letter name in the Greek translator: not present in the Greek dictionary, and Greek rules (el_rules) do not translate the symbol, so ph_buf stays empty.
Unknown-letter English fallback re-invokes SetTranslator2("en") while tr is still the Greek translator2 (reached via TranslateRules -> LookupLetter(tr, wc, -1, ...) in dictionary.c).

new_language "en" differs from translator2_language "el", so SetTranslator2 deletes the Greek translator object even though it is still the active 'tr' of the enclosing nested TranslateWord/SpeakIndividualLetters/TranslateLetter chain (use-after-free root cause).

note: After SetTranslator2 freed the Greek translator, the nested TranslateLetter continues and reads tr->langopts.accents from the freed translator: heap-use-after-free read.
